author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction is judged on the same terms as the booking, replaces that visit rather than adding one, and returns to the owner's record. It is reachable only by addressing it directly; no page links to it.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit form carrying that visit's stored date and description.
Submitting that same address with a description and a date later than today leaves that visit carrying the submitted date and description, and shows the owner's record.
Given a pet with one booked visit, when a correction to it succeeds, the pet still has exactly one visit - no second visit is created.
Submitting a blank description is refused, the description is named, the form is shown again, and the stored visit is unchanged.
Submitting a date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, the form is shown again, and the stored visit is unchanged.
Correcting a visit that does not belong to the named pet, or a pet that does not belong to the named owner, is refused rather than applied.
The owner detail page gains no link or button to the correction.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit - NG-5 keeps cancellation out of scope
Deleting a visit, a pet, or an owner - NG-4 stands
A visible entry point to the correction from the owner detail page or any other page; a later request may add one
Moving a visit to a different pet or owner
Any correction to a visit beyond its date and description
notes: NG-5 narrowed by docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowed.md; the ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md still needs adding - that file is outside product-requirements-expert write scope. Product owner fixed the correction to present the same form surface and the same refusals as the booking; the mechanism is the design stage's call. Edge cases 3-5 under Visits in docs/prd.md belong to this slice. Four open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md rather than blocking - visible entry point, confirmation message, previous-visits list on the correction page, and correcting a past-dated visit; the narrowest reading was taken for each.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction reuses the edit shape PetController already demonstrates, applied inside VisitController: a GET+POST pair on a {visitId}/edit path, with the existing @ModelAttribute resolver made conditional on an optional visitId path variable (PetController.findPet:76 is the precedent - required=false path variable, new entity when absent, entity resolved through the aggregate when present). No new package, no new type, no service layer, no repository. The one adjustment to durable memory is that a Visit's date and description are correctable after booking, which the 2026-08-27 non-goal ADR admits and which adds no lifecycle state - system-design.md State Machine stays true as written. Persistence is unchanged: OwnerRepository remains the sole write path and the correction cascades from a saved Owner. Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository and VisitController updated with REQ-VIS-003, and the aggregate-navigation invariant made explicit under Invariants the rows cannot carry. The ADR index row for the new non-goal ADR is added (docs/adr/README.md), and the 2026-08-08 row now shows the narrowing in its Status cell.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId. When null the booking behaviour is unchanged (new Visit, pet.addVisit). When non-null it returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and must NOT call pet.addVisit - that call is what would create the second visit.

Pet gains getVisit(Integer id) mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) at Owner.java:117 - iterate getVisits(), skip isNew(), Objects.equals on the id, return null when absent. Keeping the navigation in the aggregate rather than in the controller is the one place this codebase does put model logic in the model.

GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit returns "pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm" and nothing else; the @ModelAttribute has already prefilled date and description. Mirrors PetController.initUpdateForm:140.

POST on the same path mirrors processNewVisitForm minus owner.addVisit: same non-future date check rejecting on error code typeMismatch.visitDate, same result.hasErrors() redisplay, then this.owners.save(owner) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. The bound visit is the same instance held in owner's pet's visit set (both come from the one findById in loadPetWithVisit), so binding mutates it in place and the cascade issues an UPDATE. This shared-graph fact is the whole mechanism for update-in-place - do not re-resolve the owner separately and copy fields, as PetController.updatePetDetails must because it loads the owner twice.

The template needs no change. th:object=${visit} plus the inputField fragment prefills both fields; method="post" with no action posts back to the current URL, which is already the edit URL. visit['new'] is false on this path, so the heading reads "Visit" and the previous-visits table renders - both are the narrowest reading of the two open questions the PRD recorded.

patterns.description: the project's existing edit-in-place shape: optional path variable resolving the entity through the aggregate, a no-op GET handler, and a POST that validates then saves the owner
child-by-identity lookup inside the aggregate, the model for Pet.getVisit(Integer)
the existing pet-does-not-belong-to-owner guard; the visit-does-not-belong-to-pet guard mirrors it

risks.risk: The pet gains a second visit because the model-attribute method still runs new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit) on the edit path.
risks.mitigation: Branch on visitId before constructing; the non-null branch returns the resolved visit and never calls addVisit. theVisitCorrectionShouldNotAddASecondVisitToThePet is the test that pins it.

risks.risk: A refused correction leaves the rejected values in the database, because binding mutates the loaded entity in place before validation runs.
risks.mitigation: Safe as configured: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false leaves the graph detached, so nothing flushes without an explicit save, and the error path returns the view before reaching save. Do not put @Transactional on the handler and do not make the graph managed across the request - either would let dirty checking flush the rejected values. The two refusal tests assert the stored visit is unchanged, which is what keeps this honest.

risks.risk: A visitId belonging to another pet, or a petId belonging to another owner, is applied instead of refused (the mass-assignment/object-reference row of security-principles.md, and the acceptance criterion that names it).
risks.mitigation: Resolve strictly along owner -> pet -> visit from the freshly loaded owner; there is no VisitRepository, so no global by-id lookup is even reachable. Throw IllegalArgumentException as the existing pet guard does. Keep the exception message to the identifiers already present in the URL - the error page renders exception text (system-design.md Known Defects), so it must not carry anything else.

risks.risk: The identifier-binding disallow list stops covering the visit binder.
risks.mitigation: VisitController's @InitBinder is unqualified and so applies to every attribute including visit. Leave it unqualified; identity must come from the path variable only, never from a submitted field.

risks.risk: A new user-facing string is introduced and lands in one message bundle only, breaking REQ-LANG-002 and its build-time bundle-key test across all eleven locales.
risks.mitigation: Introduce no new message key. No acceptance criterion calls for a confirmation message on this path, so the narrowest reading is to add no flash attribute at all - which also sidesteps the hard-coded-English shape the existing booking flash uses.

notes: NG-5 is narrowed by docs/adr/2026-08-27-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowed.md, so this slice is not conflicting; the ADR index row the PRD expert flagged is now added. No new ADR is warranted - the mechanism is the existing feature-package pattern applied once more, easily reversible and unsurprising in context, and the product decision already carries its own ADR. Vocabulary: the docs/ubiquitous-language.md entry for Visit is unchanged and still governs; 'correction' is the verb used in the PRD and the ADR, and Appointment/Booking stay on the Avoid list. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op this dispatch. Two of the PRD's four open questions (previous-visits list on the correction page, confirmation message) are answered here by taking the narrowest reading rather than changing anything; the button label still reads 'Add Visit' on the correction page for the same reason, which a later slice can revisit once it is willing to touch all eleven bundles.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: IDOR / broken object-level authorization: verified independently. The only path to a Visit in the new handlers is owners.findById(ownerId) -> owner.getPet(petId) -> pet.getVisit(visitId) in VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:71-98). Owner.getPet(Integer) and the new Pet.getVisit(Integer) both scan only the parent's own collection and compare ids with Objects.equals, skipping unsaved entities. grep over src/main/java confirms the repository set is OwnerRepository, PetTypeRepository, VetRepository only - there is no VisitRepository and no PetRepository, so no global by-id visit lookup is reachable from any code path. A mismatched owner/pet/visit triple therefore resolves to null and throws IllegalArgumentException before any handler body runs; an attacker walking visitId cannot reach a visit belonging to another owner's pet.

Error-message disclosure: the three IllegalArgumentException messages (VisitController.java:75-76, 80-81, 94-95) interpolate only ownerId, petId and visitId - values the attacker already supplied in the URL - and no entity field, PII or internal state. src/main/resources/application.properties sets no server.error.include-message, so Boot's default (never) leaves templates/error.html's ${message} empty in the first place; even with it enabled the messages leak nothing beyond the request path.

Mass assignment: the unqualified @InitBinder at VisitController.java:53-56 (dataBinder.setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")) is controller-scoped and applies to every handler in the class, so it covers both new /edit handlers and both bound model attributes (visit and owner). Entity identity for the corrected visit comes solely from the path variable resolved in loadPetWithVisit; a POSTed id or *.id parameter cannot repoint the write. The remaining Owner-field binding surface on the edit POST is identical to the pre-existing /visits/new POST and to the owner edit form, so the new endpoint adds no writable field and no new capability.

Transaction / partial-write hazard: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false is set in application.properties, so the owner graph loaded by loadPetWithVisit is detached by the time the handler runs. On the validation-refusal path (VisitController.java:150-152) no repository call is made and no persistence context is open to dirty-check or flush the mutated in-memory Visit, so the stored visit is provably unchanged. The success path is a single owners.save(owner) whose own transaction cascades the visit UPDATE atomically; the absence of @Transactional on the handler creates no partial write.

Output escaping: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders every user-derived value (pet.name, pet.type, owner names, visit.description) through th:text, which Thymeleaf HTML-escapes; no th:utext, inlined JS, or unescaped sink was introduced. The redirect target "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}" is expanded from the int path variable, so no open-redirect or header-injection sink exists.

Supply chain: build.gradle and all dependency declarations are untouched by this change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only lists only two production Java files, one test file and docs), so no new or upgraded artifact is introduced and no CVE surface is added. dependencyCheck is not configured in this project, so no analyzer run applies.
Secret sweep over the added lines of the change set (token, password, secret, credential, api key, bearer patterns) returned no hits; no hardcoded credential or key material is introduced.
